headline: High risk of shared-repo write conflicts and prompt-injection via git-tracked files; no direct evidence of data residency mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can execute shell commands; xonsh also reads/writes the filesystem and runs shell/Python expressions. Because Aider’s outputs can land in shared repo files that xonsh may consume, a file-based instruction injection path exists in default shared-workspace use. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, file-based prompt injection is possible.
IF xonsh treats repo files as trusted input, attacker-controlled instructions can be executed or followed.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working directories.
Review any file content before xonsh consumes it.
Disable automatic execution of generated shell snippets.
Use a read-only checkout for xonsh when inspecting Aider output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for generated files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch filesystem contents and source code, and Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys via env vars. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive files to the other through the repo or shell output. There is no evidence of a stronger third-party exfiltration path, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets or private source, both agents can read them.
IF Aider writes sensitive context into tracked files, xonsh can read it from the filesystem.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Add .gitignore rules for sensitive artifacts.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can modify git state and write the shared repo, while xonsh can also write the filesystem and execute shell commands. Aider’s concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo, but xonsh has no multiple-instance support and no locking is documented. That makes concurrent writes and git-state races dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git repository concurrently, conflicting writes can occur.
IF xonsh writes files while Aider auto-commits, git history can diverge or be overwritten.
mitigations: Serialize access to the repository.
Use separate branches per agent.
Run one agent read-only during the other’s write phase.
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or a coordinator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code or shell edits that xonsh can then execute or use in notebooks, so Aider’s output may become B’s input without a documented verification step. Xonsh’s shell/Python execution makes downstream mistakes more consequential, but there is no direct evidence that it blindly trusts Aider, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF xonsh executes commands or code produced by Aider without review, errors can cascade.
IF Aider emits incorrect shell snippets, xonsh may run them in the same environment.
mitigations: Require manual review before execution.
Use dry-run mode for generated commands.
Compare outputs against a second source.
Limit xonsh to non-destructive commands during review.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and document local filesystem/source-code handling, but neither profile shows a residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch. Aider does send data to configured model providers, while xonsh lists local tooling and no special compliance boundary, so only a small compliance gap is evidenced here.
conditions: IF Aider is configured to send regulated data to an external model provider, compliance obligations may apply.
IF xonsh is used on regulated data without corresponding controls, logging/retention may be inconsistent.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared prompts.
Confirm provider terms before use.
Disable unnecessary logging.
Document data handling responsibilities.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
